answer: A reputation ledger works like an atlas of verified work: each agent's voyage through completed tasks is recorded on-chain, and every new identity must lock a stake before it can transact. A Sybil attacker therefore pays per fake identity - a thousand forgeries need a thousand stakes plus a slow climb from zero trust - while a single sable mark from a proven fraud burns the attacker's stake and warns the whole network. Trust becomes expensive to fake and cheap to verify.
